intent.raw_query: Safari Kenya family of 3, $8000, 10 days, July 2026

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in a dramatic spectacle. Game drives in open 4x4 vehicles offer close encounters with the Big Five including lions, elephants, leopards, buffaloes, and rhinos in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop
experiences.description: Observe some of Africa's largest elephant herds roaming the open plains with the iconic snow-capped Mount Kilimanjaro as a stunning backdrop. Amboseli is renowned for its large elephant populations and offers exceptional photography opportunities at sunrise and sunset.

experiences.name: Hot Air Balloon Safari over the Savannah
experiences.description: Drift silently over the vast Maasai Mara savannah at dawn in a hot air balloon, spotting wildlife from a bird's-eye perspective. The experience concludes with a traditional bush champagne breakfast in the middle of the wilderness, making it a truly unforgettable adventure.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Rhino Sanctuary Visit
experiences.description: Explore Lake Nakuru National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its vast flocks of pink flamingos coating the alkaline lake shores. The park is also a critical sanctuary for both black and white rhinos, offering excellent rhino tracking opportunities alongside diverse birdlife and other wildlife.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Maasai Village Cultural Immersion & Bush Walk
experiences.description: Engage authentically with the Maasai community through a guided village visit where you learn traditional customs, witness warrior jumping dances, and participate in fire-making and beadwork. Follow it with a guided bush walk led by Maasai warriors who share their deep knowledge of local flora, fauna, and tracking techniques.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Kenya
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and arrange budget airport transfer (matatu/shared shuttle ~KES 200-300) to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and take a relaxed orientation walk along the beachfront to get your bearings and enjoy the warm 25°C weather.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the beach at sunset. Explore the immediate resort surroundings and nearby local market stalls to get a feel for the area. Grab a light dinner close to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick, affordable bite at the airport – local chapati with beans (~KES 150)
meals.dinner: Local beachside food stall near resort – grilled fish with ugali and kachumbari (~KES 400-500)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light due to afternoon arrival. Keep cash in Kenyan Shillings (KES) handy. Exchange money at the airport or use a local ATM. Stay hydrated – warm weather expected.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning nature walk along the beach to observe coastal birdlife and marine activity. Look out for kingfishers, herons, and crabs along the shoreline. The cool morning air makes this ideal before the day heats up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local nature reserve or coastal forest trail (entry ~KES 500). Explore mangrove ecosystems and spot monkeys, monitor lizards, and tropical birds. Hire a local guide for a budget-friendly walking tour (~KES 800-1000) to maximize wildlife spotting.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort area. Visit a local village market to browse fresh produce and handmade crafts. Watch the sunset from the beach.

meals.breakfast: Resort or nearby café – mandazi (fried dough) with chai tea (~KES 150)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a local duka (small shop) – samosas and fresh fruit (~KES 200)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant near resort – nyama choma (grilled meat) with sukuma wiki and ugali (~KES 500-600)

day_by_day.notes: Wear light, breathable clothing and apply sunscreen. Bring a reusable water bottle. Tipping local guides KES 200-300 is appreciated and culturally appropriate.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day budget safari excursion – Day 1 of 2. Depart early by shared safari van (book through a budget operator ~KES 3,500-4,500 per person) toward Tsavo East or Amboseli National Park. En route, enjoy scenic savannah landscapes and roadside wildlife spotting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive inside the national park. Spot elephants, zebras, wildebeest, giraffes, and a wide variety of bird species. Amboseli offers iconic views of Mount Kilimanjaro on clear days. Bring binoculars for the best wildlife viewing experience.
day_by_day.evening: Set up at a budget campsite or basic bandas (thatched huts) near the park (~KES 1,500-2,500 per night). Campfire dinner under the stars with fellow travelers. Listen to the sounds of the African bush at night.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at resort before departure – tea, bread and eggs (~KES 200)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch prepared by tour operator or bought en route – sandwiches and juice (~KES 250)
meals.dinner: Campsite communal dinner – beans stew, rice, and vegetables (~KES 400)

day_by_day.notes: Book your budget safari operator at least 2-3 days in advance. Shared group safaris are the most cost-effective option. Pack insect repellent, a light jacket for evenings, and a camera with a zoom lens.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise game drive (5:30 AM departure) – this is the best time to spot predators like lions and cheetahs as they are most active in the early morning. Watch elephants gather at watering holes as the day begins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue afternoon game drive exploring different sections of the park. Visit a Maasai cultural village near the park boundary (~KES 500 entry) to learn about traditional wildlife conservation practices, see traditional dances, and browse handcrafted jewelry.
day_by_day.evening: Begin return journey to the resort. Arrive back by early evening. Rest and recover from the safari days. Light beach walk to decompress.

meals.breakfast: Early campsite breakfast – porridge and tea (~KES 150)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch during game drive – fruit, crackers, and water (~KES 200)
meals.dinner: Back at resort area – local restaurant serving pilau rice with chicken (~KES 450-550)

day_by_day.notes: Total safari cost for Days 3-4 including transport, park fees, and basic accommodation should be approximately KES 8,000-12,000 per person when booked as a group package. Always confirm park fees are included in your tour price.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the safari. Enjoy a slow breakfast at the resort. Spend time on the beach swimming or snorkeling in the warm Indian Ocean waters. Observe coastal marine life including colorful fish and sea urchins in the shallow reef areas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local marine conservation area or coral reef snorkeling spot (~KES 500-800 including basic snorkel gear rental). Explore the vibrant underwater ecosystem along the Kenyan coast. Look out for sea turtles, reef fish, and starfish.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner on the beach. Join locals for a game of beach volleyball or simply relax. Explore the beachfront for fresh seafood vendors.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – fresh tropical fruit platter with yogurt and tea (~KES 300)
meals.lunch: Beachside vendor – grilled corn on the cob and coconut water (~KES 150)
meals.dinner: Local seafood restaurant – grilled prawns or lobster with coconut rice (~KES 600-700)

day_by_day.notes: July is a great month for snorkeling as visibility is generally good. Apply reef-safe sunscreen to protect the coral ecosystem. Negotiate snorkel gear rental prices – KES 500 is a fair rate.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget boat trip to a nearby island or sandbar (~KES 1,000-1,500 per person on a shared dhow). Traditional Swahili wooden dhow sailing is an authentic Kenyan coastal experience. Watch dolphins that frequently accompany boats in these waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the island on foot – look for nesting seabirds, monitor lizards, and unique coastal vegetation. Swim in secluded crystal-clear waters away from the main beach crowds. Collect shells and enjoy the peaceful natural environment.
day_by_day.evening: Return to mainland by late afternoon. Visit a local Swahili cultural center or old town area if nearby. Browse local craft markets for affordable souvenirs like kikoi fabric, wooden carvings, and beaded jewelry.

meals.breakfast: Local café – chai tea with mahamri (Swahili doughnuts) (~KES 150)
meals.lunch: Picnic on the island – packed fresh fruits, bread, and local cheese bought from market (~KES 200)
meals.dinner: Swahili cuisine restaurant – biryani with coconut fish curry (~KES 500-600)

day_by_day.notes: Negotiate dhow prices as a group to reduce per-person costs. Bring extra water and snacks for the island trip. Wear a hat and light long-sleeved shirt for sun protection on the boat.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby national park or wildlife sanctuary (e.g., Shimba Hills National Reserve if on the south coast, or Arabuko-Sokoke Forest Reserve if near Malindi). Take a shared matatu or budget taxi (~KES 300-500 one way). These are UNESCO-recognized biodiversity hotspots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided nature walk through the forest reserve with a Kenya Wildlife Service ranger (~KES 600-800 including guide fee). Spot rare species including the endangered Sokoke scops owl, golden-rumped elephant shrew, and Clarke's weaver. The forest is alive with butterflies and exotic plants.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by late afternoon. Relax on the beach and watch the sunset. Write travel notes and review photos from the week's wildlife encounters.

meals.breakfast: Resort or guesthouse – scrambled eggs with toast and fresh juice (~KES 250)
meals.lunch: Forest reserve picnic area – packed lunch from local market (~KES 200)
meals.dinner: Budget local restaurant – mukimo (mashed potato with greens and corn) with beef stew (~KES 400-450)

day_by_day.notes: Arabuko-Sokoke Forest Reserve is one of Africa's most important coastal forests for biodiversity. Entry fees support conservation. Wear closed-toe shoes and long trousers for the forest walk to protect against insects.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching session at a local wetland, lagoon, or estuary near the resort. Kenya's coast is exceptional for birding with over 300 species recorded. Bring binoculars and a bird identification app. Look for flamingos, kingfishers, African fish eagles, and wading birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local community-run eco-tourism project or wildlife rehabilitation center (~KES 500 entry). Learn about conservation efforts to protect sea turtles, dugongs, and coastal wildlife. Many centers allow visitors to assist with feeding or monitoring activities.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a local cultural performance or community bonfire event on the beach. Many coastal communities organize evening cultural shows featuring traditional Giriama or Swahili music and dance (~KES 300-500 per person).

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast – banana, bread and thermos tea (self-prepared, ~KES 100)
meals.lunch: Community project café – local home-cooked meal supporting the community (~KES 350)
meals.dinner: Beachfront local eatery – whole grilled snapper with chips and coleslaw (~KES 550)

day_by_day.notes: Supporting community eco-tourism projects directly benefits local conservation efforts. Ask your resort reception for recommendations on reputable community projects in the area. Photography at cultural events – always ask permission first.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise kayaking or stand-up paddleboard session along the coastline (~KES 800-1,000 per hour rental). Paddle through calm morning waters and observe coastal bird activity from the water. This offers a unique wildlife perspective not possible from land.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby historic Swahili town, ruins, or heritage site (e.g., Gede Ruins near Watamu or Fort Jesus in Mombasa if accessible – entry ~KES 500-1,000). These UNESCO-listed sites connect Kenya's rich cultural and natural history. Hire a local guide (~KES 500) for deeper insights.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening in Kenya. Return to the beach for a farewell sunset walk. Reflect on the trip's wildlife and nature highlights. Visit a local artisan market for any last-minute souvenir shopping.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a slightly upgraded resort breakfast – full Kenyan breakfast with eggs, sausage, fruit and coffee (~KES 400)
meals.lunch: Heritage site area café or street food – mishkaki (skewered grilled meat) with kachumbari (~KES 300)
meals.dinner: Celebratory farewell dinner at a mid-range local restaurant – seafood platter to share (~KES 700-800 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to repack bags and ensure all wildlife souvenirs comply with CITES regulations – no coral, shells from protected species, or ivory products. Check your departure logistics for the following day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning – wake up early for one last beach sunrise walk. Take photos and soak in the coastal atmosphere. Complete packing and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Store luggage with reception if needed for a late departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, use remaining hours for a final light activity – a short nature walk, last-minute souvenir shopping at local markets, or simply relaxing on the beach. Arrange budget transfer back to the airport (shared shuttle or matatu ~KES 200-300).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Kenya with incredible wildlife memories, safari experiences, and coastal nature encounters. Review and organize trip photos during the journey home.

meals.breakfast: Final Kenyan breakfast at a local café – chai, mandazi and fresh mango (~KES 200)
meals.lunch: Airport or en route – light meal at a local eatery before departure (~KES 300-400)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departure. Keep some KES for airport tips and last-minute purchases. Total estimated budget for the 10-day trip (excluding international flights): KES 35,000-50,000 (~USD 270-385) per person covering accommodation, local transport, meals, activities, and park fees.

trip_options.title: Classic Kenya Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.description: Engage authentically with the Maasai community through a guided village visit where you learn traditional customs, witness warrior jumping dances, and participate in fire-making and beadwork. Follow it with a guided bush walk led by Maasai warriors who share their deep knowledge of local flora, fauna, and tracking techniques.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Rest and transfer from the airport to Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your beachfront accommodation. Take a leisurely stroll along the beach to decompress after the flight and get oriented with the resort surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed sunset walk along the shoreline. Head to the resort's beachfront area to watch the Indian Ocean sunset — a perfect gentle introduction to Kenya.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight
meals.lunch: Light snack or meal at the airport or resort welcome refreshments upon check-in
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's main restaurant — try Swahili coastal dishes such as grilled fish with coconut rice and kachumbari salad (mid-range resort dining, approx. $20–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 1.5–2 hours for airport transfer to the resort. Keep luggage light for easy access. Exchange some currency to Kenyan Shillings (KES) at the airport. No strenuous activities on arrival day — rest is key for acclimatization.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a full resort breakfast and then take a guided nature walk along the coastal forest trail near the resort. Spot coastal birdlife, vervet monkeys, and indigenous flora typical of Kenya's coastal ecosystem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local market or coastal village to get a feel for authentic Kenyan coastal culture. Browse handcrafted souvenirs, Maasai beadwork, and locally made batik fabrics. A great low-key orientation to Kenyan daily life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a beachside dinner experience. Enjoy the warm evening breeze (approx. 25°C) and watch the stars over the Indian Ocean.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at the resort — fresh tropical fruits, eggs, mandazi (Kenyan doughnuts), and chai tea
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a local coastal eatery near the market — try pilau rice with beef or vegetable curry (approx. $8–12 per person)
meals.dinner: Beachside BBQ dinner at the resort or a nearby open-air restaurant — grilled prawns, nyama choma (grilled meat), and ugali (approx. $20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the market visit. Carry a small daypack with sunscreen, water, and a hat. Weather will be warm and sunny — ideal for outdoor exploration. Tipping local guides is appreciated (approx. 500–1000 KES).

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by road or domestic flight to Lake Nakuru National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Begin your Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Rhino Sanctuary Visit with a morning game drive. Witness thousands of pink flamingos lining the alkaline lake shores and search for both black and white rhinos in the sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the afternoon game drive around Lake Nakuru. Look out for lions, leopards, Rothschild's giraffes, Cape buffaloes, and waterbucks. The golden afternoon light makes for spectacular wildlife photography.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a mid-range lodge near Lake Nakuru (e.g., Lake Nakuru Sopa Lodge or Flamingo Hill Tented Camp). Freshen up and enjoy a communal campfire dinner with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — packed breakfast box if leaving very early
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch enjoyed inside the park at a designated picnic site by the lake — included with most guided tours
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Lake Nakuru lodge — buffet-style with a mix of Kenyan and international dishes (approx. $25–35 per person, often included in lodge packages)

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru is approximately 4–5 hours by road from the coast or 1 hour by domestic flight from Nairobi. Pre-book a reputable safari operator for the game drive. July is excellent for wildlife sightings as the dry season concentrates animals near water sources. Carry binoculars for flamingo and bird watching.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive in Lake Nakuru National Park — the best time to spot predators and rhinos before the midday heat. Spend time at the lake's edge observing the flamingo flocks and pelicans in the soft morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel from Lake Nakuru to the Maasai Mara region (approximately 3–4 hours by road through the scenic Rift Valley). Check in to a mid-range Mara camp or lodge (e.g., Mara Sopa Lodge or Basecamp Masai Mara).
day_by_day.evening: Evening sundowner game drive in the Maasai Mara to catch your first glimpse of the iconic savannah landscape. Watch the sunset over the open plains and spot elephants, hippos, and big cats returning from the watering holes.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Lake Nakuru lodge before the morning game drive
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch stop at a local restaurant in Narok town during the drive to the Mara — try nyama choma and chapati (approx. $10–15 per person)
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the Maasai Mara lodge or camp — traditional Kenyan cuisine with a safari ambiance around a campfire (approx. $25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The road from Nakuru to Maasai Mara passes through Narok — a good stop for fuel and refreshments. Pack a light fleece or jacket as Mara evenings can be cooler than the coast. Ensure your lodge is booked well in advance as July is peak Great Migration season and accommodation fills quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari begins at dawn. Join a guided game drive to witness the world-famous Great Migration — millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles thundering across the plains. July is prime time for dramatic Mara River crossings where crocodiles lie in wait.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the game drive deeper into the Mara ecosystem. Search for the Big Five (lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, rhino) and enjoy a bush lunch in the field surrounded by wildlife. The afternoon light is perfect for spotting cheetahs on termite mounds scanning for prey.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp for a hot shower and rest. Gather around the campfire for a guided talk by your safari guide about the Great Migration ecosystem, predator-prey dynamics, and conservation efforts in the Mara.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-dawn breakfast at camp — coffee, toast, eggs, and fruit before the morning game drive
meals.lunch: Bush picnic lunch in the Mara — packed by the lodge with sandwiches, fruit, and juice enjoyed in the field
meals.dinner: Dinner at camp — three-course meal with soup, main course (roasted chicken or beef stew), and dessert by candlelight (included in most lodge packages)

day_by_day.notes: July is peak Great Migration season — river crossings are most frequent in the afternoon. Ask your guide to position near the Mara River crossing points early. Wear neutral-colored clothing (khaki, olive, brown) for game drives. Do not stand up or make sudden movements in the safari vehicle near predators.

day_by_day.morning: Hot Air Balloon Safari over the Savannah — depart before dawn for this once-in-a-lifetime experience. Drift silently over the vast Maasai Mara at sunrise, spotting wildebeest herds, elephants, and big cats from a bird's-eye perspective. The golden sunrise over the savannah is absolutely breathtaking.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the balloon safari (which typically ends mid-morning with a champagne bush breakfast), return to camp for rest. Take a leisurely afternoon to relax, review wildlife photos, or enjoy a guided walking safari near the camp perimeter with an armed ranger.
day_by_day.evening: Maasai Village Cultural Immersion experience — visit a traditional Maasai boma (village) near the Mara at dusk. Participate in traditional dances, learn about Maasai warrior culture, beadwork, and cattle herding traditions. A deeply authentic and memorable cultural exchange.

meals.breakfast: Champagne bush breakfast included with the hot air balloon safari — served on linen-covered tables in the open savannah (a highlight of the trip)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the camp — salads, sandwiches, and fresh juice
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Maasai village or back at camp — try traditional Maasai cuisine including fermented milk (mursik) and roasted goat meat (approx. $15–20 additional if dining at the village)

day_by_day.notes: The Hot Air Balloon Safari must be pre-booked well in advance — cost is approximately $450–550 per person but is a truly unmissable experience. Dress warmly for the balloon flight as it is cold at altitude before sunrise. The Maasai village visit typically costs $20–30 per person as a community fee — money goes directly to the village.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning game drive in the Maasai Mara — focus on any wildlife you haven't yet photographed. Spend time at the Mara River watching for hippos and crocodiles. Say farewell to this extraordinary ecosystem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel from Maasai Mara to Amboseli National Park (approximately 5–6 hours by road via Nairobi, or arrange a scenic domestic charter flight). Check in to a mid-range Amboseli lodge (e.g., Ol Tukai Lodge or Amboseli Serena Safari Lodge).
day_by_day.evening: Evening game drive in Amboseli with the iconic backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro glowing in the last light of day. Spot elephants gathering at the swamps as the mountain turns pink and orange at sunset — one of Kenya's most iconic scenes.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Mara camp before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch stop in a town en route or at a roadside lodge — try a local Kenyan buffet with rice, beans, sukuma wiki (collard greens), and chicken (approx. $10–15 per person)
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the Amboseli lodge — enjoy the view of Kilimanjaro illuminated by lodge lights while dining on Kenyan cuisine (approx. $25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: If flying between parks, domestic charter flights are available through operators like SafariLink or AirKenya — approximately $150–250 per person and saves significant travel time. July weather in Amboseli is dry and clear — ideal for Kilimanjaro views which are best in the early morning and evening.

day_by_day.morning: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop — begin at dawn for the best Kilimanjaro views before clouds build. Observe some of Africa's largest elephant herds (Amboseli is home to over 1,500 elephants) roaming the open plains with the snow-capped peak towering behind them. A truly iconic African scene.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the game drive focusing on Amboseli's diverse wildlife — lions, cheetahs, wildebeest, zebras, and hundreds of bird species around the Enkongo Narok swamp. Visit the Observation Hill for a panoramic view of the entire Amboseli basin and Kilimanjaro.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks on Observation Hill or at the lodge — watch the famous Amboseli elephant herds silhouetted against Kilimanjaro as the sun sets. An unforgettable photographic moment.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn breakfast at the lodge before the morning game drive — keep it light: coffee, fruit, and toast
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the field near the Enkongo Narok swamp — enjoy watching elephants and hippos while eating
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge — try a three-course meal featuring Kenyan-inspired dishes such as Amboseli lamb stew with ugali and roasted vegetables (approx. $25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli elephants are habituated to vehicles and can be observed at very close range — keep noise to a minimum and engines off when possible. The best Kilimanjaro views are between 06:00–09:00 before clouds obscure the peak. Bring a telephoto lens for elephant portrait photography.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning game drive in Amboseli — focus on the elephant families and their calves in the golden morning light. Visit the Cynthia Moss Elephant Research Camp area (if accessible) to learn about decades of elephant behavior research in Amboseli.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel back to the coast and Aegean Bliss Resort (approximately 5–6 hours by road or 1 hour by domestic flight). Arrive in time for a relaxing beachside afternoon swim and sunset. Decompress after an action-packed safari week.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the safari journey with a special dinner at the resort's finest restaurant or a nearby upscale coastal eatery. Reflect on the incredible wildlife experiences over a beautiful Indian Ocean dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Amboseli lodge before checking out
meals.lunch: Lunch en route — stop at a local town restaurant or pack a lunch box from the lodge
meals.dinner: Celebratory seafood dinner at a coastal restaurant near the resort — fresh lobster, grilled snapper, and Swahili coconut curry with a glass of South African wine (approx. $30–45 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the return flight or transfer in advance. If driving, the Amboseli–Mombasa road via Tsavo is scenic and passes through Tsavo East National Park — keep eyes open for wildlife from the vehicle. Arriving back at the coast allows for two full relaxation days before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy a long leisurely breakfast by the beach. Take a final swim in the Indian Ocean and soak up the warm Kenyan sun (25°C). Visit the resort spa for a relaxing massage or treatment as a final treat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at a nearby coastal craft market — pick up Maasai beadwork, wooden carvings, kikoi fabrics, and locally roasted Kenyan coffee to bring home. Pack your bags and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the resort — choose your favorite dish from the week or try something new from the Swahili menu. Spend the last evening on the beach watching the stars over the Indian Ocean and reminiscing about 10 extraordinary days in Kenya.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final breakfast at the resort — full buffet with fresh tropical fruits, Kenyan chai, eggs made to order, and fresh-baked pastries
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch at the resort's poolside café — grilled fish tacos, fresh coconut water, and a fruit platter (approx. $12–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the resort restaurant — Swahili feast with biryani, grilled seafood, kachumbari, and mandazi for dessert (approx. $25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight details and arrange airport transfer in advance (allow 2–3 hours before flight time). Kenya's departure tax is typically included in international tickets but verify with your airline. Declare any wildlife products at customs — it is illegal to export ivory, certain animal skins, or live animals. Leave a tip for resort staff who made your stay special (approx. 1,000–2,000 KES per staff member is appreciated).

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in a dramatic spectacle. Game drives in open 4x4 vehicles offer close encounters with the Big Five including lions, elephants, leopards, buffaloes, and rhinos in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop
experiences.description: Observe some of Africa's largest elephant herds roaming the open plains with the iconic snow-capped Mount Kilimanjaro as a stunning backdrop. Amboseli is renowned for its large elephant populations and offers exceptional photography opportunities at sunrise and sunset.

experiences.name: Hot Air Balloon Safari over the Savannah
experiences.description: Drift silently over the vast Maasai Mara savannah at dawn in a hot air balloon, spotting wildlife from a bird's-eye perspective. The experience concludes with a traditional bush champagne breakfast in the middle of the wilderness, making it a truly unforgettable adventure.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Rhino Sanctuary Visit
experiences.description: Explore Lake Nakuru National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its vast flocks of pink flamingos coating the alkaline lake shores. The park is also a critical sanctuary for both black and white rhinos, offering excellent rhino tracking opportunities alongside diverse birdlife and other wildlife.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County

experiences.name: Maasai Village Cultural Immersion & Bush Walk
experiences.description: Engage authentically with the Maasai community through a guided village visit where you learn traditional customs, witness warrior jumping dances, and participate in fire-making and beadwork. Follow it with a guided bush walk led by Maasai warriors who share their deep knowledge of local flora, fauna, and tracking techniques.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Nairobi Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to meet you at the arrivals hall with a personalized welcome sign.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Nairobi airport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a scenic drive through the Kenyan countryside. Check in and settle into your beachfront suite with a welcome cocktail and resort orientation tour. Take a leisurely stroll along the beach to decompress after your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on your private terrace or at the resort's infinity bar overlooking the ocean. Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the resort's signature restaurant, savoring fresh Swahili coastal cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport lounge)
meals.lunch: Light refreshments provided during private airport transfer — artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, and chilled beverages in the vehicle
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature oceanfront restaurant — fresh grilled lobster, Swahili-spiced prawns, and locally sourced seasonal produce paired with premium Kenyan wines

day_by_day.notes: Flight LH lands at 13:00. Allow approximately 1.5–2 hours for immigration, baggage, and customs. Private transfer driver will be waiting in arrivals. Resort check-in is typically 14:00–15:00; early check-in can be pre-arranged. Unpack and rest — this is a recovery day.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the resort followed by a guided nature walk along the beachfront and coastal forest trail with a resident naturalist. Spot coastal bird species, monitor lizards, and indigenous flora unique to Kenya's Indian Ocean coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Resort-arranged private snorkeling or glass-bottom boat excursion over the nearby coral reef. Alternatively, enjoy a luxury spa treatment — a traditional Swahili massage using locally sourced coconut and baobab oils — to fully recover from jet lag.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cruise along the coast on a traditional dhow, watching the golden sunset over the Indian Ocean with canapés and champagne. Return to resort for a private beachside dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at the resort's ocean-view dining terrace — fresh tropical fruits, made-to-order eggs, Kenyan chai, and freshly baked pastries
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort's beach club — grilled catch-of-the-day, avocado salads, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Private beachside dinner under a canopy of stars — a curated 5-course tasting menu featuring Swahili-spiced seafood, mango coulis dessert, and premium South African Chenin Blanc

day_by_day.notes: Weather expected to be warm at around 25°C with minimal rainfall — ideal for coastal activities. Apply reef-safe sunscreen for all water activities. Tip your naturalist guide generously as is customary.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private charter flight from the coast to the Maasai Mara (approximately 1.5 hours). Arrive at a luxury tented camp airstrip and transfer to your exclusive Mara camp. Enjoy a bush breakfast before your first game drive into the Maasai Mara National Reserve.
day_by_day.afternoon: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari — witness the world-famous spectacle of millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles crossing the Mara River. Your private guide and open-top 4x4 Land Cruiser provide unrivaled access to the action. Look out for big cats — lions, cheetahs, and leopards — hunting along the migration routes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the luxury tented camp for hot bush showers and sundowner drinks around a fire pit under the vast Mara sky. Dinner in the open-air dining tent with fellow safari guests and your guide sharing wildlife stories.

meals.breakfast: Bush breakfast served in the field — freshly brewed Kenyan coffee, scrambled eggs, bacon, and fresh fruit laid out on a linen-covered table in the savannah
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the bush — gourmet hamper with artisan breads, cold cuts, cheeses, and fresh juices served under an acacia tree
meals.dinner: Three-course dinner at the luxury tented camp dining pavilion — slow-braised game stew, roasted root vegetables, and a decadent chocolate fondant, paired with premium Kenyan coffee

day_by_day.notes: Pack lightweight, neutral-colored safari clothing (khaki, olive, beige). Bring a quality pair of binoculars and a camera with a telephoto lens. July is peak Great Migration season — river crossings are highly likely. Minimum two game drives recommended per day for the best sightings.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for the Hot Air Balloon Safari over the Savannah — drift silently at sunrise over the vast Maasai Mara, spotting elephant herds, lions on kills, and the sweeping migration from 300 meters above. A truly once-in-a-lifetime perspective lasting approximately 1 hour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-balloon champagne bush breakfast in the field — a classic Mara tradition. Return to camp for a midday rest during the heat of the day. Optional guided walking safari with an armed Maasai ranger around the camp perimeter to learn about tracking, medicinal plants, and smaller wildlife.
day_by_day.evening: Maasai Village Cultural Immersion — visit a traditional Maasai boma near the reserve boundary. Participate in jumping ceremonies, learn fire-making techniques, browse handcrafted beadwork, and share stories with community elders. Return to camp for a spectacular bush dinner.

meals.breakfast: Celebratory champagne bush breakfast immediately after balloon landing — smoked salmon blinis, fresh fruit platters, pastries, and sparkling wine in the open savannah
meals.lunch: Light lunch back at camp — chilled gazpacho, grilled chicken wraps, and tropical fruit sorbet
meals.dinner: Maasai-inspired bush dinner at camp — nyama choma (grilled meats), ugali, sukuma wiki, and roasted corn, served around a traditional fire with Maasai warriors as honored guests

day_by_day.notes: The balloon safari departs approximately 05:30 — an early night is strongly recommended. Balloon rides are weather-dependent; your camp will confirm the evening before. Dress in warm layers for the balloon as early morning temperatures at altitude can be cool. Bring cash (USD) for Maasai craft purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning game drive in the Maasai Mara focusing on the northern conservancies — less crowded and home to exceptional predator activity. Search for the elusive leopard in riverine forest areas and observe cheetah families on the open plains with your expert private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to camp for lunch and a guided photography masterclass with the camp's resident wildlife photographer. Learn composition techniques, camera settings for fast-moving animals, and golden-hour shooting strategies using the afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drive to a scenic Mara hilltop viewpoint with chilled gin and tonics, local snacks, and a 360-degree panoramic view of the reserve at dusk. Night game drive back to camp spotting nocturnal species — aardvark, genets, and bush babies.

meals.breakfast: Full English breakfast at camp — eggs benedict, grilled tomatoes, mushrooms, and freshly squeezed passion fruit juice
meals.lunch: Poolside lunch at camp — chilled avocado soup, grilled tilapia, and a selection of Kenyan artisan cheeses
meals.dinner: Candlelit dinner under the stars at camp — pan-seared duck breast, truffle mashed potatoes, and a decadent crème brûlée, paired with a fine Bordeaux

day_by_day.notes: The northern Mara conservancies (Olare Motorogi, Mara North) offer exclusive game viewing with very few vehicles. Night drives are not permitted inside the main reserve but are available in private conservancies — confirm with your camp. Bring a red-light headlamp for nighttime camp navigation.

day_by_day.morning: Morning game drive with a focus on the Mara River crossing points — July is peak crossing season and witnessing thousands of wildebeest plunge into crocodile-infested waters is one of Africa's greatest wildlife spectacles. Position early and wait patiently with your guide for the crossing to begin.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private charter flight from Maasai Mara to Amboseli (approximately 1.5 hours). Transfer to your luxury Amboseli lodge with sweeping views of Mount Kilimanjaro. Settle in and enjoy an afternoon game drive in Amboseli National Park.
day_by_day.evening: Amboseli Elephant Watching at sunset — observe Africa's largest elephant herds silhouetted against the iconic snow-capped peak of Kilimanjaro as the sun sets behind it. This is one of the most photographed scenes in all of Africa. Return to lodge for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast at the Mara camp before departure — granola, yogurt, fresh fruit, and strong Kenyan coffee
meals.lunch: In-flight snack box on charter flight, or welcome lunch at Amboseli lodge upon arrival — fresh salads, grilled meats, and fresh juices
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Amboseli lodge's open-air restaurant — roasted lamb rack with rosemary jus, seasonal vegetables, and a classic lemon tart, paired with a Kenyan Pinot Noir

day_by_day.notes: Mara River crossings are unpredictable — patience is key. Your guide will read animal behavior to anticipate crossings. Amboseli is at a higher altitude than the coast — evenings can be cooler. Pack a light fleece. Kilimanjaro views are often clearest in the early morning and late afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Backdrop — a full morning dedicated to tracking Amboseli's legendary elephant families, including some of the largest tuskers in Africa. Your guide will introduce you to specific elephant family groups by name, sharing their individual histories and behaviors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Amboseli Research Centre to learn about the long-running elephant research project — one of the world's longest continuous wildlife studies. Meet a resident researcher for a private briefing. Followed by a guided walk to an Amboseli swamp area to spot hippos, buffalo, and waterbirds.
day_by_day.evening: Maasai Bush Dinner — a special private dinner set up in the bush with Maasai warriors standing guard around a lantern-lit table. Enjoy a curated menu while listening to the sounds of the African night and learning about Maasai astronomy and star navigation.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast on your private lodge deck — freshly baked croissants, tropical fruit, smoked salmon, and Kenyan estate coffee while watching elephants on the plains below
meals.lunch: Lodge lunch — chilled cucumber soup, grilled chicken with chimichurri, and fresh mango sorbet
meals.dinner: Private Maasai bush dinner — slow-cooked lamb shoulder, roasted sweet potatoes, and traditional Kenyan stews served by candlelight in the wilderness

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli is dusty — bring a buff or light scarf to cover your face during game drives. The elephant families here are accustomed to vehicles and will approach very closely — an extraordinary experience. Book the private bush dinner at least 24 hours in advance through your lodge concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive in Amboseli with a focus on predator activity — lions, hyenas, and wild dogs are active at dawn. Photograph elephants against Kilimanjaro in the magical early morning light before the haze builds. Return to lodge for a full breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private charter flight from Amboseli to Lake Nakuru (approximately 1 hour). Transfer to your luxury lodge overlooking the lake. Afternoon game drive in Lake Nakuru National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site — spotting white and black rhinos, Rothschild giraffes, and vast flocks of flamingos.
day_by_day.evening: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Rhino Sanctuary sunset experience — watch tens of thousands of pink flamingos create a shimmering carpet of color along the lake's shoreline as the sun sets. Return to lodge for a celebratory dinner marking the midpoint of your safari journey.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast — eggs any style, fresh fruit, Kenyan tea, and freshly baked breads served on the lodge veranda
meals.lunch: Packed lunch enjoyed at a scenic viewpoint within Nakuru Park — gourmet wraps, fruit salad, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at the Nakuru lodge — slow-roasted beef tenderloin, truffle risotto, and a classic tiramisu, paired with a premium Tuscan Chianti

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru is one of Kenya's best parks for rhino sightings — both white and black rhino are present. The flamingo numbers vary seasonally but July typically offers excellent viewing. The park is also home to Rothschild giraffe, one of the world's rarest giraffe subspecies. Bring your binoculars for birdwatching.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning game drive in Lake Nakuru National Park with a dedicated focus on rhino tracking with a specialist ranger. Visit the rhino sanctuary area for close-up encounters with these magnificent endangered animals. Also look for leopards in the yellow fever tree forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private charter flight back to the Kenyan coast (approximately 1.5 hours). Return to Aegean Bliss Resort for a luxurious final coastal stay. Spend the afternoon relaxing by the pool or enjoying a premium spa treatment — a hot stone massage or Hammam ritual.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell sundowner cocktails on the beach. Private romantic dinner on the beach — a specially curated menu celebrating the flavors of Kenya's coast, served at a table set directly on the sand with lanterns and flower petals.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast before departure — continental spread with fresh fruits, pastries, and Kenyan coffee
meals.lunch: In-flight snack on charter, then welcome-back light lunch at Aegean Bliss Resort — fresh seafood ceviche, tropical salad, and chilled coconut water
meals.dinner: Private farewell beach dinner — a 7-course tasting menu featuring Kenyan coastal delicacies: crab bisque, grilled Mombasa prawns, Swahili fish curry, and a passion fruit pavlova, paired with vintage Champagne

day_by_day.notes: Confirm charter flight timings the evening before. Allow time to pack safari clothing and ensure all wildlife souvenirs comply with customs regulations — no ivory, no wildlife products. The farewell beach dinner must be pre-arranged with the resort concierge at least 48 hours in advance for the best setup.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk along the beach with a resort naturalist — a peaceful farewell to Kenya's Indian Ocean coastline. Spot coastal birds, collect shells, and reflect on the incredible wildlife experiences of the past 10 days. Return for a leisurely last breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Late checkout arranged (subject to availability) — enjoy a final swim, spa treatment, or simply relax in your beachfront suite. Private luxury transfer to the nearest airport for your departure flight. Resort concierge handles all luggage and check-in logistics.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Kenya. Your private transfer ensures a smooth, stress-free airport experience with dedicated porter service and fast-track check-in assistance where available.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — a full à la carte menu featuring your favorite dishes from the trip, freshly squeezed juices, and a farewell cake from the resort's pastry chef
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the resort before transfer — grilled snapper, fresh salad, and a final glass of Kenyan sparkling wine
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dinner or in-flight dining (business/first class recommended for the return journey)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure transfer timing with the resort concierge the evening before. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for international departures from Kenyan airports. Consider purchasing premium Kenyan coffee, tea, and locally made crafts as gifts at the airport. Tipping: budget approximately USD 10–15 per day per guide and USD 5–10 per day for camp/lodge staff as a collective tip envelope.

query: Safari Kenya family of 3, $8000, 10 days, July 2026
